the Christian cross.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Vingthor is given as another name for Thor; Thor is associated with the hammer Mjollnir, and Jorth/Earth and Othin are identified as his mother and father.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Loki is separately noted, and Laufey is dwarfs.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Heimdall is described through the phrase 'whitest of the gods'; the note connects him with light, watchmanship, wisdom, and sleepless watching over all the worlds.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The Wanes are mentioned in relation to knowledge of future events, though the note says they are not elsewhere described as especially gifted in that way.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Thor's wagon is said to be always drawn by goats; Jotunheim OF HYNDLA / INTRODUCTORY NOTE / FRAGMENT OF THE SHORT VOLUSPO / NOTES; lines 9273-9311","start":"9273","end":"9311","translation":"The Poetic Edda","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"Editorial notes discuss lacunae and manuscript repetitions around stanzas 42-49; identify or cross-reference figures including Loki, Fenrir, Sleipnir, Mithgarthsorm, Angrbotha, Freyja, Hyndla, Ottar, Angantyr, Heithrun, and others; summarize an obscure myth in which Loki eats a cooked woman's heart and gives birth to a monster; note a world-destruction passage, a possible Christian reference, Freyja's revelation that her boar is Ottar, the memory-beer used for genealogical recall, and a reconstructed threat by Freyja to burn a giantess unless she fetches the memory-beer.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The notes state that there is probably a lacuna before stanza 42 and probably an omission before stanza 44; stanza 49 may also have lost two lines.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:3","ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Fenrir is identified as a wolf born of Loki and the giantess Angrbotha.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Sleipnir is identified as Othin's eight-legged horse, born of the stallion Svathilfari and Loki in the guise of a mare.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Mithgarthsorm is identified as another child of Loki and as the likely referent of the phrase glossed as 'the worst.'","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Loki, also called Lopt, is said to eat the cooked heart of a woman and then himself give birth to a monster in a myth otherwise not further known.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"A cited Snorri account is summarized as making the wolf, the serpent, and Hel children of Loki and Angrbotha.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The notes refer readers to another passage for the description of the destruction of the world.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The notes say a possible reference to Christianity is discussed elsewhere and that the fragmentary short Voluspo ends before the Freyja-Hyndla dialogue continues.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Freyja admits that her boar is Ottar, who is to use memory-beer to recall a genealogy and win a wager with Angantyr.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"Heithrun is identified as the she-goat by Valhall, while the name is said to be used here for she-goats in general in a caustic comment on Freyja's morals.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"The manuscript is said to repeat lines by mistake in stanza 49.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"The notes reconstruct the likely lost sense of two lines as Freyja threatening to burn the giantess alive unless she quickly fetches the memory-beer.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Loki / Lopt","description":"Named as Loki or Lopt; associated with GROUGALDR / GROAS SPELL; lines 9359-9466","start":"9359","end":"9466","translation":"The Poetic Edda","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"At the doors of the dead I call thee","summary":"Svipdag summons his dead mother Groa at a death-threshold and asks for help. He says a false woman associated with his father has sent him to seek Mengloth where no one may go. Groa chants a numbered sequence of protective charms against journey dangers, enemies, fetters, sea storms, frost, night curses, and verbal strife with a giant, then tells him to keep her words within him.","language":"English","quote_policy":"quoted"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Svipdag calls on Groa, identified as his good mother, at the doors of the dead and asks for help at the hill of death.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Groa replies as Svipdag's mother, calls him her only son, and says she lies in the mould and has left the world of the living.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Svipdag says a false woman whom his father embraced set him a baleful task: to go where none may fare and seek Mengloth the maid.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Groa says the way is long, the wandering long, love is also long, and success depends on the favor of the fates.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Svipdag asks his mother to chant good charms and guard him because he fears death on the way and considers himself young.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Groa's first charm is described as an often-tried charm that Rani taught to Rind; it lets Svipdag shake off what mislikes him and become his own helper.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Groa's second charm protects Svipdag if he must travel a purposeless road by making the bolts of The brothers settle at Ulfdalir by Lake Ulfsjar, find three Valkyrie women with swan-garments spinning flax at the shore, bring them home, and live with them for seven winters. King Nithuth learns of his isolation, seizes a ring and sword, has Vlund bound and hamstrung, and confines him to Svarstath to smith precious objects. Vlund later lures Nithuth's sons, kills them, and turns parts of their bodies into ornaments sent to Nithuth's household. Bothvild then comes to Vlund about her broken ring.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Hlathguth and Hervor are identified as Hlothver's children, and Olrun the Wise is identified as Kjar's daughter.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"One woman takes Egil in her arms, Swan-White is said to wear content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.norse-poetic-edda-bellows-gutenberg-l13146-l13224","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/norse/project-gutenberg/poetic-edda-bellows.md","passage_locator":{"label":"NOTES / FRA DAUTHA SINFJOTLA / OF SINFJOTLIS DEATH / INTRODUCTORY NOTE; lines 13146-13224","start":"13146","end":"13224","translation":"The Poetic Edda","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"The passage recounts Sinfjotli’s killing of Borghild’s unnamed brother, Borghild’s revenge by poisoned ale at a funeral feast, Sinfjotli’s death, and Sigmund’s carrying of his body to a fjord where a man in a little boat takes the corpse away and disappears. It then transitions to Sigmund’s later marriage to Hjordis, the birth of Sigurth, Sigmund’s death in battle, and Sigurth’s exceptional heroic status. The appended note comments on manuscript blanks, variant traditions, and the possible identity of the boatman as Othin.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Sigmund is presented as son of Volsung, king in the land of the Franks, and father of Sinfjotli, Helgi, and Hamund.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Sinfjotli and Borghild’s unnamed brother woo the same woman, and Sinfjotli kills the brother.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Borghild asks Sinfjotli to depart, but Sigmund offers atonement-money, which Borghild has to accept.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"At a funeral feast, Borghild repeatedly brings Sinfjotli ale in a horn that contains poison.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Sinfjotli recognizes the drink as poisoned and warns Sigmund; She explains Odin's sleep-punishment, gives Sigurth mead or beer associated with memory and runes, and teaches categories, uses, origins, inscriptions, and distribution of runic knowledge before offering him a choice of speech or silence.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Sigurth rode up Hindarfjoll, turned southward, and saw a great light like burning fire whose glow reached heaven.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"At the place of the light, Sigurth found a tower of shields with a banner above it.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Inside the shield-tower Sigurth found a sleeping figure with war-weapons; after removing the helm he saw that the figure was a woman.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The mail-coat was fast to the sleeper's flesh; Sigurth cut it open and removed it, after which she awoke and sat sword.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"After Sigurth asked her name, she gave him a horn full of mead described as a memory-draught.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"She hailed day, night, gods, goddesses, and earth, and asked that wisdom, good speech, healing hands, and victory break.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"The passage identifies her as Sigrdrifa, a Valkyrie; she killed Hjalmgunnar in battle after Othin had promised him victory, seats.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:16","text":"The poem says old written runes were shaved off, mixed with holy mead, and sent widely so that gods, elves, Wanes, and a son to die, and Gunnar's troubled consultation with Hogni.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The introductory note says the poem bears storytelling.","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The introductory note says the poem drew on prose and verse material, other Eddic poems, lost poems, and prose variants.","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Sigurth seeks Gjuki, is called a young Volsung and battle victor, trusts two brothers, and joins them under mighty Slim and Tur, fearing Minchihr's vengeance, send gifts and a message of repentance, blaming Iblis and offering obedience. Feridn rejects the attempted reconciliation, displays his warriors, refuses to exchange blood for gold, and declares that Minchihr will punish the brothers for Irij's The brothers advance toward Irn with a large army. Feridn waits strategically, appoints commanders, and Minchihr stands at the center under the sacred banner of the blacksmith. Tr challenges Minchihr's legitimacy; Kabd accuses the brothers of murdering Irij, and Minchihr declares that he seeks vengeance for Irij. After a bloody battle, Minchihr is victorious with Heaven's favor. He defeats a night attack, kills Tr, sends Tr's head to Feridn, pursues Slim to a fort, and kills the warrior Kak after Kak's failed sally.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"A messenger returns trembling to Slim and Tr and reports Minchihr's appearance, his warriors, delay.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Slim and Tr collect armies from both kingdoms and proceed toward Irn, while Feridn orders his army to wait quietly for / ZL, THE SON OF SM / THE DREAM OF SM / RDBEH; lines 2812-2927","start":"2812","end":"2927","translation":"Persian Literature, Volume 1","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"The passage recounts the discovery of a disguised emissary connected to Rdbeh and Zl, Rdbeh's confession of love to her mother Sndokht, Mihrb's angry response, Minchihr's alarm over the political and ancestral implications of the match, Sm's report of victories over a Zohk-descended enemy and demons, Minchihr's command to destroy Kbul and Mihrb's house, and Sm's letter asking mercy while recalling his past service, especially the slaying of a devastating dragon.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"A questioned emissary is found with sirbund and male attire and refuses to betray the secret, instead claiming to be a dealer in jewels and dresses.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Sndokht goes to her daughter's apartment to learn the matter.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Rdbeh openly tells Sndokht that she loves Zl, has met with him, and has pledged mutual love with him.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Rdbeh reports that Sm has consented to the nuptials with Zl.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Mihrb becomes enraged when he learns of the arrangement and fears the resentment of Sm and Minchihr.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Mihrb draws a dagger and intends to rush to Rdbeh's chamber, but Sndokht falls at his feet and restrains him.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Rdbeh appears before Mihrb in jewels and splendid apparel rather than removing her ornaments as an offender or supplicant.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Mihrb describes the situation with images of a devil united to an angel and a snake killed in Arabia.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Minchihr is concerned that the union of Zl and Rdbeh may bring confusion and ruin to Persia because Mihrb descends from Zohk.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"Feridn is said to have purified the world from the abominations of Zohk.","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"Sm recounts defeating a ruler descended on the mother's side from Zohk and causing the demon army to flee or submit.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"Minchihr orders Sm to destroy Kbul by fire and sword, especially Mihrb's house, and to kill Mihrb, described as of the serpent-race, and his adherents.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"Sm attempts to dissuade Minchihr from revenge but does not change his decision.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"The news of Minchihr's intentions creates alarm in Mihrb's family at Kbul.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:15","text":"Zl returns to Sm, and Sm sends a letter to Minchihr by Zl as messenger to deprecate the king's wrath.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:16","text":"In the letter, Sm recalls his long service, martial prowess, and the destruction of a mighty monster.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:17","text":"The monster's jaws depopulate half the land, create widespread terror, and leave no bird, beast, crocodile, eagle, or human inhabitant alive in the affected country.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:18","text":"Sm describes the monster as huge as a mountain, with hideous hair, a long black tongue blocking the path, eyes like lakes of blood, a terrifying roar, and poison issuing from its mouth.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]},{"id":"obs:19","text":"Sm wounds the monster with arrows through the tongue, throat, and middle, then kills it with a cow-headed battle-axe blow to the brain.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:11"]},{"id":"obs:20","text":"After the monster dies, the world regains peace and comfort.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:11"]},{"id":"obs:21","text":"Sm states that he is old and that it is fitting to resign his station to Zl.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:12"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"the emissary","description":"A person questioned about sirbund and male attire who claims to be a dealer in jewels and dresses and does not reveal the secret.","role_refs":["role:1"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"Sndokht","description":"Rdbeh's mother, who questions the situation, goes to Rdbeh, restrains Mihrb, and brings Rdbeh before him after receiving a promise of safety.","role_refs":["role:2","role:3"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:3","ev:4"]},{"id":"fig:3","name_or_label":"Rdbeh","description":"A daughter who declares her love for Zl, says they have pledged mutual love, reports Sm's consent, and appears before Mihrb adorned in jewels and splendid letter to Minchihr.","role_refs":["role:6","role:7"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:8","ev:12"]},{"id":"fig:5","name_or_label":"Sm","description":"A warrior and father of Zl who has returned from content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.persian-persian-literature-volume-1-gutenberg-l2929-l3036","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/persian/project-gutenberg/persian-literature-volume-1.md","passage_locator":{"label":"MINCHIHR / ZL, THE SON OF SM / THE DREAM OF SM / RDBEH; lines 2929-3036","start":"2929","end":"3036","translation":"Persian Literature, Volume 1","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"A child will be born of mighty power, who will become the wonder of the world.","summary":"Sindokht secures Sam's support for Zal and Rudabeh's marriage through an embassy with rich gifts. Minuchihr consents after consultation with astrologers, who predict a heroic child. Rudabeh suffers dangerously near childbirth; Zal burns the Simurgh's feather, and the Simurgh appears, predicts the child's greatness, and gives saving advice. Rustem is born prodigiously strong and rapidly matures. His grandfathers Sam and Mihrab celebrate him, while Sam prays that Rustem become a benefactor rather than a tyrant.","language":"English","quote_policy":"quoted"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Mihrab believes the threatened desolation of his country can only be avoided by putting his wife Brmn.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Brazen drums on elephants signal departure, and Afrsiyb's army advances rapidly until it reaches Kai-ks sends word to Zl for help; Zl commissions Rustem, who chooses the shorter road filled with dangers, demons, and sorcery, prepares Rakush, receives his mother's farewell, and departs from Sstn to free the captive king.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Gw comes near the city and finds it splendid, crowded with adorned women and damsels, with a treasure-chamber full of gold and jewels and a country abundant in cattle.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Information about Mzindern is sent to Kai-ks, who is delighted and regards the region as blessed and beautiful.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The king of Mzindern responds to the invasion by calling the gigantic White Demon to his aid.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"At night a cloud, pitch-like darkness, and tremendous hailstones fall upon the Persian host, causing destruction, flight, and confusion.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Kai-ks loses sight, his treasury is captured, and his army is killed or taken prisoner.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"After seven days of affliction, Kai-ks hears the White Demon roar a taunting speech about his folly, his lack of an army, and the White Demon's power.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Twelve thousand demon-warriors are selected to guard the Irnian captives, who are bound and given only enough food to keep them alive.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Arzang, a demon-leader, takes possession of Kai-ks's wealth, crown, and jewels and escorts the blinded captive king and troops to Mzindern.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Kai-ks sends an account of his blind and helpless captivity to Zl, laments ignoring Zl's advice, and asks for rescue.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"Zl privately instructs Rustem to take up the sword, saddle Rakush, and undertake the rescue because Zl's old age prevents him from bearing the war effort.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"Zl explains that one road to Mzindern is long, while the shorter road is full of dangers, lions, demons, and sorcery and may bring Rustem there in seven days.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"Rustem chooses the short road despite its danger, compares it to a way toward hell and a tiger's lair, and states his trust in God for victory.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"The next day Rustem puts on war attire, prepares his horse Rakush, parts from his sorrowing mother Rdbeh, and departs from Rustem asks that Sohrb's host be protected and allowed to return home, and Ks agrees to end the war. The armies depart; Rustem conducts sacrificial funeral rites, leads the bier in procession through Zbul, and receives the mourning of Zl, Rdbeh, and the public. Sohrb's body is displayed, covered with a yellow robe, enclosed in an aloe bier, and commemorated by a hoof-shaped sepulchral mound. News reaches Trn, Afrsiyb's realm, Samengn, and finally Tahmneh, who laments her son, his search for his father, and the unshown bracelet that might have prevented his death.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Ks joins Rustem in mourning and speaks of death as inevitable and the past as unrecoverable.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Rustem asks that Sohrb's unguided host be protected, removed from war, and allowed to retrace their way toward their mountain-wilds and the Jihn waters.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Ks agrees that the war shall cease, and the Tartar legions return to their homes.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Persian warriors gather around the dead, grovel in dust, shed tears, and then the monarch leads them back to Irn.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Rustem remains with his native bands and maintains further sacrificial rites in which a thousand horses are bled and torn drums are scattered on the sand.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"A mournful procession moves through Zbul; Rustem walks before the bier, and his warrior-friends assemble near it.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Zl and his kindred join the funeral train; Rustem identifies the dead as his offspring, and Zl responds with astonishment and bloody tears.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Rdbeh loudly laments the dead stripling, whose youth is described as sheltered in his mother's arms before seeking his father and dying.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Rustem reopens the bier and exposes Sohrb to public view; husbands, wives, warriors, old and young gather, tear garments, loosen hair, shriek, and weep.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"The mourners cry that Sohrb sleeps as Sm the Champion Manjeh invites him into her tent, where he is received with luxury and feasting for three days. Afrsiyb’s advisers redirect the duel into a general attack, and Barz is surrounded until Rustem, Fermurz, and Kai-khosru come to his aid. replacements.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Afrsiyb challenges Kai-khosru to single combat, proposing that the two rulers decide the deceitful.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Kai-khosru assigns another expedition against Trn to Gdarz after saying Rustem has already AND AFRSIYB / THE EXPEDITION OF GDARZ / THE DEATH OF AFRSIYB / THE DEATH OF KAI-KHOSRU; lines 10639-10741","start":"10639","end":"10741","translation":"Persian Literature, Volume 1","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"Kai-khosru turns from sovereignty to devotion, resists the pleas of nobles, Zl, and Rustem, reports a mysterious warning that his departure is near, distributes wealth and offices, appoints Lohursp as successor, announces a dream-revealed fountain where he will surrender his life, and begins his final journey while companions mourn.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Kai-khosru becomes attached to a religious life, thinks only of devotion to God, abandons the duties of sovereignty, and commits state affairs to ministers.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Chiefs and warriors respectfully remonstrate and ask him to divide his day between ruling and religious exercises.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Kai-khosru refuses the request and says that one heart is not equal to both duties, that his affections are not for the transitory world, and that he trusts to inhabit the world to come.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The people ask Zl and Rustem to intervene, saying that an evil eye or Ibls has led the king astray and darkened the country with sorrow.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Kai-khosru tells Zl and Rustem that he is weary of life’s troubles and anxious to prepare for a future state.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Kai-khosru reports that a mysterious voice told him that the time of departure is near, that he should prepare the load for the journey, and that he should not neglect the warning angel.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Kai-khosru says the palace is not the place for him and that he must seek a solitary cell where he will resign his soul to heaven.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The next day Kai-khosru gathers his great men and warriors, declares that he resigns the pageantry of kings, and says farewell.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Kai-khosru orders tents pitched in the desert, opens his treasury, holds a seven-day feast, and distributes food and money to the indigent, widows, orphans, and destitute persons.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"Kai-khosru grants territories and offices: Rustem receives Zbul, Kbul, and Nm-rz; Lohursp is appointed successor; Gdarz is appointed chief minister; Gw receives chief command of the armies; Ts receives Khorassn; and Frburz is told to obey Lohursp.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"Some warriors murmur that the son of Kai-ks should be placed under Lohursp, but after Kai-khosru praises Lohursp as enlightened and qualified, the warriors express satisfaction.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:8","ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"Kai-khosru says that in his dreams a fountain has been pointed out and that, when he visits it, his life will be resigned to its Creator.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"Kai-khosru bids farewell, begins his journey, pitches his tent after one stage, resumes travel the next day, and takes leave of Zl and Rustem, who weep bitterly.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"Zl and Rustem lament that no mortal has trod the supernal way and, while living, seen the face of God.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:11"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Kai-khosru","description":"King who renounces sovereignty for devotion, distributes royal goods and
